idiom_name: scala.concurrent.Future fan-out with flatMap/sequence on an ExecutionContext; parallel collections for data-parallel leaves
implementation_notes: Futures carry the fork/join: Future { ... } submits work to the implicit ExecutionContext and the result is joined by mapping/flatMapping the returned Future, so a recursive split becomes a tree of composed futures instead of worker objects; scala.concurrent's default ExecutionContext is ForkJoinPool-backed, and a dedicated pool should be used for CPU-bound recursion. Parallel collections (.par) cover the data-parallel lane but live in a separate module since 2.13. Blocking inside a Future consumes pool threads (scala.concurrent.blocking lets the pool compensate), so keep leaves CPU-bound.
pitfalls: Every flatMap needs an implicit ExecutionContext: reusing the global one for CPU-bound recursion competes with all other futures in the process - define a dedicated pool.
Await.result inside a Future parks a pool thread and can deadlock the ForkJoinPool; compose the futures instead of blocking on them.
Parallel collections are a separate dependency on 2.13+: mixing .par with an ExecutionContext obscures where the work actually runs.
